summary: Owner requested a granular opt-in agentic search track and implementation of its first saved archive slice. Ordinary search must remain the default.
Traced indexed revision retrieval, visibility policy and the existing offline model adapter on main. Reproduced cited ordinary retrieval on a synthetic saved document using Python 3.15.2.

Python 3.15.2 baseline passed with 371 Python tests and 12 skips, 19 station tests, and 96 Node tests. The final 19 focused tests, compile checks, CLI help and leak gate passed. The module CLI executed a checksum-pinned fixture planner, recovered the expected saved revision and preserved the database SHA-256.

Two independent reviews confirmed lazy opt-in, current eligibility, read-only lookup, original citations and failure outcomes. Added the roadmap link to task ownership and retained an explicit outcome for a malformed model manifest.

Implemented the saved-catalogue CLI and verified ordinary search, one opt-in local rewrite, restricted revisions and fallback. Hosted acceptance is recorded in the pull request. T2 and T3 remain planned.
Owner requested direct WARC intake and a real local model comparison with ordinary search as the default.
Confirmed the shared WARC framing and checksums. Selected a new read-only source intake path with atomic catalogue publication and explicit handling.

Independent panel identified ambiguous same-name archive cites, digest handling for valid transfer-coded and segmented records, and standard revisit forms. Added durable input IDs and focused regressions. Verified block integrity remains enforced for skipped records.

18 focused Python 3.15.2 tests passed. Verified plain and multi-member gzip input, SHA-1 Base32 and SHA-256 digests, equal-basename inputs, corrupt payload rejection, protected output, nonpublic skips, standard revisits, and non-2xx chunked records. Both new module commands passed on the same saved HTML WARC with an identical file SHA-256.
Completed new catalogue intake for eligible saved WARC text with explicit handling, provenance and skip counts.
Fixed a six-document, 11-query WARC corpus. Acquired the repository-locked Scout model and b10819 runner into an isolated temporary local workspace and verified their digests before inference.

Panel verified identical literalized FTS input and required separate non-target and citation checks. The runner hashes resolved assets outside timed queries and was executed with the native-bundle manifest shape. Intake hold resolved by verifying payload integrity independently of HTTP status and testing chunked non-2xx.

Ran the locked Qwen2.5 1.5B Scout and llama.cpp b10819 on Darwin arm64. Both modes recovered 3/3 exact and 0/6 paraphrased questions, correctly left 2/2 out-of-scope queries empty, and returned zero incorrect citations. Scout made 8 calls with two invalid rewrites. Median observed latency was 0.21 ms ordinary and 8365.05 ms agentic. Verified the receipt source fingerprints.
Recorded a replayable synthetic corpus and native measurement receipt. Ordinary remains the default. The measured result does not justify expanding the fallback on this corpus.
Full baseline passed on Python 3.15.2 with 377 Python tests, 12 capability skips, 19 station tests, and 96 Node tests. Leak gate and strict track health passed.
